3.2 Attentive Statistics Pooling (ASP)
For both layer- and time-wise pooling, we adopt channel- and context-dependent attentive statistics pooling
[9] provided by the SpeechBrain toolkit [22].
An overview of the process is provided in component (2) of Figure 1.
Input features are first projected into a low dimensional space via a Time-Delay Neural Network [26] (TDNN) block.
After the TDNN block, the Tanh activation function is applied.
To capture channel-specific attention, the feature representations are projected back to the original feature dimensionality through a 1D convolution with a kernel size of 1, transforming them into attention scores.
Subsequently, the softmax function is applied along the time dimension independently for each channel, resulting in temporal importance weights.
Using these normalized attention weights, the pooling mechanism computes the weighted mean and weighted standard deviation of the input features over time.

6 Conclusion
In this work, we investigated the impact of layer-wise and time-wise ASP mechanisms using features extracted from a W2V2-based model.
Our results indicate that intelligibility is more effectively modeled with layer-wise representations, whereas imprecise consonants, harsh voice and monoloudness are better captured with time-wise modeling. For inappropriate silences, no clear advantage could be observed for either group. Furthermore, an analysis of attention weights reveals that layer-wise attention distributions vary with the severity of the speech descriptors, suggesting that different severity levels activate distinct layers.
A comparison between single-layer and multi-layer time-wise ASP experiments reveals that inter-layer information still plays an important role for certain descriptors, even though time-wise ASP provides more informative representations than layer-wise ASP for these descriptors. This observation motivates future work on combining layer-wise and time-wise ASP.

IV Conclusion 
This paper investigated angle-based transmit beamforming for single-carrier underwater acoustic communications. Experimental results using the SPACE and MACE datasets demonstrated reliable single-user communication under different environmental and motion conditions, achieving low data-detection mse and zero bit errors in the tested cases. A multi-user experiment further showed support for simultaneous asynchronous transmissions through principal-path beamforming and null steering. These results demonstrate the potential of angle-based transmit beamforming for practical underwater acoustic systems, even with long feedback delays.
